name: iROC
aliases: Intracorporeal Robot-Assisted Radical Cystectomy vs Open Radical Cystectomy
question: Does robot-assisted radical cystectomy with intracorporeal urinary diversion increase days alive and out of hospital during the first 90 days compared with open radical cystectomy?

arms.label: Robot-assisted radical cystectomy with intracorporeal urinary diversion

design.population: Adults with nonmetastatic bladder cancer suitable for either surgical approach at nine UK cancer centers.
design.description: Multicenter, unblinded, phase 3 randomized superiority trial
design.locator: JAMA PDF pp2093–2095, Methods and Figure 1

verdictNote: The 2.2-day adjusted gain met significance; its clinical importance remains uncertain.
takeaway: Robot-assisted radical cystectomy with intracorporeal diversion increased 90-day days alive and out of hospital versus open cystectomy (median 82 vs 80; adjusted difference 2.2 days, 95% CI 0.50–3.85); the clinical importance of this difference remains uncertain.

reports.label: 90-day recovery and morbidity
reports.citation: Catto JWF, Khetrapal P, Ricciardi F, et al. "Effect of Robot-Assisted Radical Cystectomy With Intracorporeal Urinary Diversion vs Open Radical Cystectomy on 90-Day Morbidity and Mortality Among Patients With Bladder Cancer: A Randomized Clinical Trial." *JAMA.* 2022;327(21):2092-2103. doi:10.1001/jama.2022.7393
reports.followUp: 90-day primary endpoint; median 18.4 months for recurrence and survival
reports.followUpLocator: JAMA PDF pp2097,2100, Primary Outcome and Oncological and Survival Outcomes

results.endpoint: Days alive and out of hospital
results.measure: Median days during the first 90 days; effect is adjusted difference in log back-transformed days, robotic minus open
results.note: Modified intention-to-treat analysis in 305 of 317 operated patients, by randomized group; mixed model adjusted for center and diversion type. The prespecified superiority test used two-sided P < 0.05.
results.locator: Full text, Statistical Analysis, p 2094; Figure 1, p 2095; Primary Outcome, p 2097

results.note: Secondary outcomes were interpreted as exploratory because of multiple comparisons.
results.locator: Full text, Outcomes, p 2094; Oncological and Survival Outcomes, p 2100

results.note: Secondary outcomes were interpreted as exploratory because of multiple comparisons.
results.locator: Full text, Outcomes, p 2094; Oncological and Survival Outcomes, p 2100

results.endpoint: Generic health-related quality of life at 5 weeks
results.measure: EQ-5D-5L mean-score difference, open minus robotic; 5-week completed outcomes
results.note: Exploratory secondary comparison; no multiplicity-adjusted threshold. Completed outcomes: 130 robotic and 116 open; arm-level score point estimates are not tabulated in the main article. Difference was no longer statistically significant by 12 weeks.
results.locator: Full text, Quality of Life, p 2098; Figure 3A, p 2099

results.measure: WHODAS 2.0 mean-score difference, open minus robotic; 5-week completed outcomes
results.note: Exploratory secondary comparison; no multiplicity-adjusted threshold. Completed outcomes: 114 robotic and 102 open. Full-text Results give 0.43, whereas the abstract gives 0.48; 12-week difference was 0.38 (95% CI 0.09–0.68; P=0.01).
results.locator: Full text, Disability, pp 2098–2100; Figure 3C, p 2099

harms.label: Thromboembolic complication within 12 weeks
harms.note: Risk difference −6.47 percentage points (95% CI −11.43 to −1.38); exploratory secondary comparison.

harms.label: Wound complication within 12 weeks
harms.locator: Full text, Table 2 and Adverse Events, p 2098
harms.note: Risk difference −11.72 percentage points (95% CI −18.59 to −4.58); table and body give 17.3% for open surgery, while abstract says 16.0%.

harms.label: Ureteroileal stricture within 12 weeks
harms.locator: Full text, Table 2, p 2098, footnote b
harms.note: Reported within the genitourinary complication category; numerator not specified in the article.

harms.label: Death within 90 days
harms.note: Two deaths in the robotic group and four in the open group.

harms.label: Clavien-Dindo grade III–V complication within 12 weeks
harms.note: Calculated from mutually exclusive maximum grades III, IIIa, IIIb, IV, IVa, IVb and V in Table 2; grading data available for 151 and 150 patients.

harms.label: Infection complication within 12 weeks
harms.note: Difference −9.73 percentage points (95% CI −19.47 to 0.24); exploratory secondary comparison.

delivery.label: Cystectomy performed
delivery.note: Includes crossover; 157 and 149 patients underwent the assigned robotic and open approach, respectively.

delivery.label: Ileal conduit reconstruction
delivery.note: The remaining patients had continent diversion/neobladder.

delivery.label: Standardized surgery and recovery
delivery.value: Accredited surgeons; robotic operators had completed at least 30 cystectomies; both arms used enhanced recovery and at least external iliac, obturator, and internal iliac lymphadenectomy.

reports.label: 90-day economic evaluation
reports.citation: Dixon S, Hill H, Flight L, et al. "Cost-Effectiveness of Robot-Assisted Radical Cystectomy vs Open Radical Cystectomy for Patients With Bladder Cancer." *JAMA Netw Open.* 2023;6(6):e2317255. doi:10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2023.17255
reports.followUp: 90-day cost and quality-adjusted life-year horizon; sensitivity projections to 1 year
reports.followUpLocator: JAMA Netw Open full text, Methods, Cost-Effectiveness Analysis; Table 2

results.note: UK National Health Service perspective; equipment, theatre, ward, and complication costs included.
results.locator: JAMA Netw Open full text, Table 2, Primary analysis

results.locator: JAMA Netw Open full text, Table 2, Primary analysis; Methods, Outcomes

results.measure: Cost per QALY gained over 90 days
results.note: At a £20,000/QALY threshold, the modeled probability of cost-effectiveness was 16.3%.
results.locator: JAMA Netw Open full text, Table 2, Primary analysis

delivery.label: Economic analysis cohort
delivery.value: 305 patients with available primary outcome data from the randomized trial
delivery.locator: JAMA Netw Open full text, Abstract, Results; Methods, Statistical Analysis

relations.note: RAZOR tested robotic cystectomy with extracorporeal diversion; iROC tested a complete intracorporeal approach with recovery as the primary endpoint.
